newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Aug 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Aug 6.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The first dose of economic shock therapy is administered with the suspension of 42 finance firms and moves to increase taxes and utility charges. The measures are among conditions for an International Monetary Fund rescue package involving an initial credit line of about $15 billion. (BANGKOK POST, THE NATION)

- Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh's tough decision to implement harsh economic measures might have soured his ties with Deputy Chart Pattana leader Korn Dabaransi, who abruptly left a cabinet meeting upon learning of the closure of 42 more finance firms. A stunned Korn left the weekly meeting and never returned after Chavalit rejected his request for a review of the decision on the finance companies. (THE NATION)

- Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh has cooly brushed aside the rumour that coup makers held him in custody yesterday. Chavalit says both the military and the police are firmly behind the government. The public understands the need for painful measures to rescue the economy. (BANGKOK POST)

- ASEAN countries must strive for better coordination of their monetary policies now that two member nations - Thailand and the Philippines - have been forced to seek financial and policy-making help from the International Monetary Fund, a professor from Chulalongkorn University says. Sompop Manasangsan suggests ASEAN members cooperate in setting their financial and monetary policies to maximise their regional competitiveness to prevent speculative currency attacks. (THE NATION)

- International Trade Information (Thailand) Co - a joint government-private sector venture - will be dissolved after failing to find a market niche. Samart Corp has managed the financially-troubled company but after five years the directors decide to dissolve ITIC and are now waiting for shareholder approval. (BANGKOK POST)
